samir: heads up — I ran the new replay harness against the embedding/ranker endpoint and we got a weird p99 spike after the kernel switch. can someone sanity-check?

marta: which kernel switch? the auto-kernel selector flipped to `int8-batched-v3` on the 2pm deploy?

samir: yeah that one. baseline (fast-fp16) vs int8-batched-v3. traffic: 10k qps synthetic vs 4k qps replay (customer trace).

eli: quick numbers? p50/p95/p99/p999 for both?

samir: synthetic (batch cap 128): p50 18ms, p95 42ms, p99 90ms, p999 210ms. replay (batch cap 32, real arrival): p50 22ms, p95 85ms, p99 320ms, p999 1.2s.

zara: huge tail on replay. does replay preserve user-level batching? are we sending multiple embeddings per request?

samir: yes replay mirrors production: typical request=rerank payload with 16 candidates (vector dim 768) so per-request batch ~16 vectors. synthetic test was packing aggressively into 128.

ben: that could explain it — int8-batched-v3 has better throughput at large batch sizes but worse single-request latency under small, frequent batches because kernel launch overhead + quant conversion.

bench-bot: note — cache warmth: replay run started cold (KV cache miss ~72%), warmed to ~88% after 10m. synthetic run started warm (cache hit ~98%).

samir: good catch. I captured profiling traces. flame: `user-space -> runtime scheduler` dominated under replay. KV lookup latency spiked ~8-12ms for cold misses.

marta: can you paste the minimal reproducer flags?

samir: sure: 
```
./bench --mode=replay --trace=customerA.json --batch-cap=32 --concurrency=200 --kernel=auto --kv-cache=enabled --kv-populate=live
./bench --mode=synth --qps=10000 --batch-cap=128 --kernel=int8-batched-v3 --kv-cache=prewarm
```

eli: two things to test: 1) force kernel to fast-fp16 with replay arrival pattern, 2) force batcher to lower latency mode (dynamic max_wait 5ms).

zara: also try disabling quant for small batches: add a threshold so int8 only used when batch_size >= 64. we had heuristics like that in the old runtime.

ben: I ran quick A/B with `--kernel=fast-fp16` on same replay trace: p99 dropped from 320ms -> 110ms, p999 1.2s -> 420ms. throughput steady.

samir: interesting — so kernel choice is a major factor for the tail. but what's causing the intermittent 1.2s p999? I saw thread contention in the profiler at the acceptor queue.

bench-bot: log snippet: `[2026-11-02T14:12:31Z] batcher_wait=18ms, kernel_launch=6ms, kv_lookup=11ms, lock_wait=312ms`

eli: that lock_wait is concerning. looks like a serialization point in the KV cache population when miss-rate is high. we should collect stack traces for lock holders.

marta: adding to that, the replay harness triggers many slightly different keys so cold misses cause concurrent upstream calls to the store. consider singleflight on miss or per-shard locks.

samir: created a quick patch that gates int8 selection based on `batch_size >= 64 && kv_hit_rate >= 80%`. ran local replay: p99 135ms, p999 470ms. better but still higher than fast-fp16.

zara: what's the vector dim? bigger dims change kernel perf characteristics (memory bandwidth bound).

samir: dim=768 in these runs. I also tried dim=1024 synthetic — int8 shines there for throughput but tail still bad for small arrival patterns.

ben: we should update the kernel selector to use an arrival-pattern-aware heuristic, not only avg batch size. e.g., if observed inter-arrival jitter high -> prefer low-latency kernel.

eli: agreed. propose three signals: recent effective_batch_size p50/p95, kv_hit_rate, and inflight_request_count. use weighted scoring to pick kernel.

marta: for benchmarking methodology: we must ensure apples-to-apples: run both kernels with identical arrival traces, same cache state (cold/warm), and same per-request payload distribution. record both aggregate and per-request lat buckets.

samir: added to checklist: 1) run replay with `--seed` deterministic arrival ordering, 2) snapshot KV state and restore for each experiment, 3) run at least 10m warm-up, 4) sample flame traces at tail events.

bench-bot: reminder — include embedding dim and payload byte-size in metadata: `dim=768`, `avg_payload=3.2KB`, `candidates=16`, `request_rate=4k qps`

zara: one more angle — payload size variation. some customers have large metadata per candidate (10–20KB) which increases serialization costs and pushes kernel scheduling. can we synthesize payload-size histogram in harness?

samir: yes I'll add `--payload-hist=customerA_hist.json`. early tests show p99 increases ~40% when avg payload goes from 3KB -> 12KB due to memcpy and deserialization.

ben: action items: 
- samir: run deterministic replay forcing `fast-fp16` and `int8-batched-v3` with identical cache snapshots and payload histogram. attach profiler and lock-holder stacks.
- marta: prototype kernel-selector rule using p95 batch size + kv_hit_rate signal.
- eli: look into singleflight/lock sharding for KV populate to reduce lock_wait spikes.
- zara: extend harness to support payload histograms and candidate-size skew.

samir: will run experiments tonight, post results in this thread. if someone beats me to it, ping. :coffee:

bench-bot: experiment queued: id=exp-20261102-2130, notify=@samir @marta on completion.

zara: thanks — this is the kind of cross-cutting perf work we need to avoid surprise tails in prod.

samir: yup — goal: reduce p99 by at least 2x for replay-like traffic without losing large-batch throughput.

ben: also keep an eye on cost delta when disabling quantization for small batches — could be small but worth measuring.

samir: got it. I'll include tokens/sec and GPU-util in the report.

ci-bot: build status — bench harness branch `replay-kernel-guard` passed CI smoke tests.
